anatomy.intro: Broad upper windows bring light into the grey-green leaf body, above a compact root system.

parts.function: Two thickened leaves form one water-storing head.
parts.label: Paired fleshy leaves

parts.function: Translucent areas admit light to tissue inside the leaves.
parts.label: Upper windows

parts.function: Replacement growth and flowers emerge between the leaves.
parts.label: Central fissure

parts.function: A taproot and finer roots anchor the head and absorb water.
parts.label: Root system

flowers.text: Typical L. salicola flowers are white, a useful distinction from yellow-flowered lookalikes. After successful pollination, a Lithops seed capsule opens when wet so raindrops can splash seeds outward, then closes again as it dries.

growth.note: Inspect the grey and tan heads individually as each moves through leaf replacement.

stages.text: The visible head holds water in its two fleshy leaves.
stages.title: Current leaf pair

stages.text: A new body develops inside and uses reserves from the older pair.
stages.title: Replacement within

stages.text: Old tissue becomes a dry sheath around the replacement growth.
stages.title: Renewed head

habitat.text: Lithops salicola is native to South Africa’s Northern Cape and Free State. It grows on low limestone ridges and slopes, sometimes beside brackish pans, where its small grey body blends into the surrounding ground.

image.alt: One grey-green Lithops head with numbered fleshy leaves, olive windows, fissure and taproot.
image.prompt:
Create a square 1024px botanical educational illustration on warm ivory. Clean botanically accurate pen-and-watercolor, muted forest-green, sage and ochre palette, generous whitespace, large central specimen. Exactly four large numbered circular markers 1, 2, 3, 4 with thin clear noncrossing leader lines to the specified features. Numerals legible at 350px display. No title, words, paragraphs, watering icons, calendar, border or logo. Schematic anatomy, not a photograph of an owned plant. Show ONE representative Lithops salicola-type grey-green head with broad oval relatively open olive window surfaces, pale grey margins, smooth grey sides and a central fissure splitting exactly two succulent leaves. One head only, no cluster, no flowers. Three-quarter view above soil with schematic exposed taproot and fine side roots below a small broken soil line; never another plant attached. Marker1 to fleshy grey leaf side; marker2 to olive upper translucent window; marker3 precisely to central fissure; marker4 to root system below. Rounded low body with flatter tops, not Pleiospilos globes. Probable species illustration, not diagnostic proof.
Final refinement: Edit the supplied botanical illustration. Preserve composition, grey leaf sides, root diagram, ivory background, all four numbered markers and leader endpoints exactly. Change ONLY both top window surfaces: make the olive-green areas broad, continuous, mostly open windows with only sparse pale flecks and a pale grey margin. Remove the dense maze of pale islands across the windows. Representative Lithops salicola, not lesliei. No new features.

lookalikes.name: Lithops olivacea
lookalikes.text: Also has open olive windows, but typically produces a yellow flower with a white center.

lookalikes.name: Probable Lithops lesliei
lookalikes.text: Some forms have open windows too; the tan patterned neighbors are another possible comparison.

mature.text: Small heads can multiply into a low clump as new leaf pairs replace older ones. Compare the top view over time to see changes in head number, window pattern and the direction of each fissure.

milestones.text: Purchased at Home Depot in Howell, Michigan, from Altman Plants nursery stock.
milestones.title: Home Depot arrival

milestones.text: Moved into the Blush Mauve planter with the other appearance group; all four heads were described as firm.
milestones.title: Shared repot

nameStory.text: SANBI’s 2018 assessment lists wild L. salicola as Near Threatened, with habitat loss to crop cultivation affecting its restricted range.
